d1_pit.finding: ASYMMETRIC U-shape: GT falls ABOVE ensemble 23.4% of the time in the top decile (expected 10%). The ensemble is biased LOW and too narrow. This is NOT a symmetric under-dispersion — it is a DIRECTIONAL under-prediction.

d2_per_cell.spatial_pattern: Strong column gradient: column 0 (low moneyness) has 78-95% coverage; column 3 (high moneyness) has 45-76% coverage. The model systematically underestimates IV at high moneyness.
d2_per_cell.finding: Coverage failure is SPATIALLY CONCENTRATED. 8 of 25 cells are below 70%. The worst cells (column 2-3) drag the overall average from ~85% to 75%.

d3_per_horizon.finding: Coverage is WORST at h=1 (65.9%) and improves by h=10 (77.6%), then plateaus. No horizon reaches 90%. The h=1 deficit means the FIRST FRAME already has insufficient spread — this is not an accumulation problem.

d4_spread_vs_error.finding: Ensemble needs 45% more spread on average. Deficit is roughly constant across horizons (1.37 at h=1, 1.31 at h=30), confirming the narrowness is set at the FIRST STEP and maintained.

d5_conditional_coverage.finding: Coverage deficit is REGIME-INDEPENDENT. The model correctly scales spread proportionally to regime (1.56x spread ratio vs 1.50x error ratio). The problem is not regime adaptation — it is a universal scale deficit.

d6_ensemble_size.finding: Coverage DOES improve significantly with K (63% to 75%). At K=8 during training, the 5th/95th percentile quantiles are estimated from only the min and max of 8 samples — badly biased inward. This contributes ~5-7pp of the deficit at test time even with K=50.

d7_crps_decomposition.finding: MAE/spread ratio = 2.51 (calibrated ~2.0). With afCRPS alpha=0.95, effective loss = 0.975*MAE - 0.475*spread. MAE coefficient is 2.05x spread coefficient. CRPS gradient incentivizes narrowing the ensemble.

d8_bias.finding: STRONG SYSTEMATIC DOWNWARD BIAS: Ensemble median is 0.014 below GT (relative bias = -31% of spread). In 22 of 25 cells, GT is above the ensemble median more than 50% of the time. Most cells: median above GT only 28-45% of the time.

mechanistic_cause.summary: THREE interacting mechanisms cause 75% coverage instead of 90%

mechanism_1_bias.description: SYSTEMATIC DOWNWARD BIAS: The ensemble median is 0.014 below GT (relative bias = -31% of spread). The model systematically underpredicts IV, especially at high moneyness (column 3: coverage 45-76%). This shifts the entire distribution downward, causing GT to fall above the ensemble 90% CI upper bound 16.7% of the time (expected 5%). Bias alone accounts for ~8pp of the 15pp deficit because even with perfect spread, a shifted center misses coverage on one side.

mechanism_2_underdispersion.description: INSUFFICIENT SPREAD from afCRPS gradient structure: MAE/spread ratio = 2.51 (calibrated ~2.0). The afCRPS loss with alpha=0.95 creates effective weights 0.975 on MAE vs 0.475 on spread — a 2.05:1 ratio favoring accuracy over diversity. The model converges to an ensemble that is 45% too narrow. Correcting bias alone would bring coverage to ~83%, not 90%. The residual deficit is pure spread.

mechanism_3_finite_k.description: FINITE-SAMPLE QUANTILE BIAS: With K=8 during training, the empirical 5th percentile = min(8 samples) and 95th = max(8 samples). These are biased inward: E[min of 8] > true 5th percentile. The model learns to produce a distribution whose empirical quantiles are calibrated at K=8, but at test time with K=50 the quantiles expand, partially compensating. Still, the learned distribution itself is too narrow because CRPS with K=8 penalizes spread more than with K→infinity.

mechanistic_cause.spatial_concentration: The deficit is NOT uniform across the IV surface. Column 3 (high moneyness) has 45-76% coverage while column 0 (low moneyness) has 78-95%. This suggests the model struggles with the right tail of the moneyness distribution where IV dynamics differ (e.g., skew behavior). The per-cell bias is largest at cell (0,0) = -0.075 and (0,4) = -0.052.
mechanistic_cause.regime_independence: Critically, the deficit is regime-independent (calm=73.0%, turb=73.0%). The model correctly adapts spread to regime (1.56x). The problem is a universal SCALE factor on spread, not conditional adaptation.
actionable_implications: Increase spread_weight from 0.5 to ~0.7 to rebalance MAE/spread gradient ratio toward 2.0
Increase K during training from 8 to 16-20 to reduce finite-sample quantile bias
Add asymmetric bias penalty: the model systematically underpredicts, especially at high moneyness cells
Consider cell-specific spread scaling: column 3 needs ~2x more spread than column 0
